messages:
alex: Noticing a pattern: the Go SDK quickstart for generator streaming uses context.Background() when creating the client. Folks are canceling the request ctx and expecting streams to shut down, but we see goroutine pileups in prod sample apps.

keiko: Oof. Using Background for request-scoped streams is definitely the root cause in many of these reports. We should update the quickstart to demonstrate passing the request context into the client or generator and show an explicit cancel/timeout. Short example: 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 20*time.Second)
defer cancel()
client := redwood.NewClient(apiKey) // client ok to be long-lived
gen := client.Generator(ctx, req)
defer gen.Close()
for gen.Next() { // handle tokens }
```
Note: prefer client methods that accept ctx rather than binding ctx into client creation for global clients.

matt: There's also a problem in the retry/backoff helper: during exponential backoff we sleep without observing ctx.Done(). So even if the request context is canceled, the retry loop can block for the full backoff and keep goroutines alive. I sketched a patch to select on ctx.Done() while waiting and added a small jitter that uses time.NewTimer + select on timer.C and ctx.Done().

alex: Nice. Can you drop that in a PR? Also update the docs quickstart + an inline note in generator docs: "Always create streams with request-scoped contexts and call Close() in a defer."

leo: On ergonomics: the generator stream type exposes Close(), but other streaming types use CloseStream() in our public packages. We should standardize on Close() for all stream-like types to reduce cognitive friction in sample apps. If we change the name, add a short migration note in the Go SDK CHANGELOG.

keiko: Agreed. For the immediate customer-facing fix, docs + retry change is enough. For the API rename we'll schedule a follow-up (major/minor semver implications).

matt: Also adding a unit that asserts no goroutine leak after cancel helps catch regressions. Test plan: start generator in goroutine, cancel ctx, wait ~50ms, assert goroutine count back to baseline (accounting for test helpers). I can add that to streaming_test.go.

ci-bot: CI: build passed on branch fix/go-retry-cancel (job #6912) :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks all. TL;DR for the docs PR: replace Background() sample, show request ctx with timeout, show defer gen.Close(), call out the retry backoff change, and link the test that asserts no goroutine leak. I'll file the short issue for the Close() vs CloseStream() API parity so we can discuss.

keiko: One more note: quickstart users often copy the minimal snippet into handlers that already have r.Context(). Emphasize "use r.Context() or a derived context, not context.Background()" in the sidebar. That subtle wording prevents a lot of pain.

alex: Great point. I'll push the docs PR and assign reviewers @keiko @matt. Once CI passes we'll roll to staging.
